The three core primitives form a hierarchical weather influence model: first, venue type sets deterministic environmental bounds (dome vs. outdoor); second, wind orientation introduces directional stochasticity through azimuth-based kernel computation; third, data fusion enriches the model with additional meteorological variables. These operators interact in a layered fashion—dome games are filtered out of wind-dependent effects, while outdoor games undergo directional analysis. The failure mode occurs when wind direction is misaligned with stadium orientation, leading to underestimation of crosswind impact. Dualities emerge in that indoor environments decouple from atmospheric forces, whereas outdoor ones couple with them. Each primitive must be verified against empirical weather station data to maintain calibration integrity.
